answer: Stake-weighted selection makes splitting pointless. Each validator locks coins in an on-chain vault, and every epoch a public randomness beacon picks block proposers with probability proportional to locked stake, not to the number of accounts. Ten accounts holding 100 coins each win exactly as often as one holding 1,000, so extra identities add fees but no rewards. Coins arriving over a bridge count only after source-chain finality, so one deposit cannot be counted twice. Limitation: wealth still buys influence.
